root_cause.text: The `v3d_get_extensions()` function iterates over a userspace-supplied singly-linked list of extensions without any length bound, and an empty multisync extension (zero `in_sync_count` and `out_sync_count`) bypasses the duplicate-extension guard, enabling a self-referential `next` pointer to cause an infinite loop in kernel context.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message detail the infinite loop attack: a local user can craft a self-referential extension (`ext->next == &ext`) with zero sync counts, and the existing guard `if (se->in_sync_count || se->out_sync_count) return -EINVAL` never fires because `v3d_get_multisync_post_deps()` returns immediately without updating the counts when count is zero. The patch adds an early rejection of empty multisync extensions (`!multisync.in_sync_count && !multisync.out_sync_count`) to break the loop.
